QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H is 0.482, slightly below 0.5 for independent, finite-variance returns. R²=0.928 describes fit only across scales 8–63. Short and long slopes (0.462 and 0.569) differ enough that one line fits poorly across those scales. This may reflect crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Absolute-return H=0.774 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H rose 0.018 over one observation and 0.027 over five. It’s 0.16 standard deviations above its prior-30 baseline, not a significance test because windows overlap. H/alpha moved from 0.520/3.300 (Nov 6) to 0.482/3.378 (Nov 20).

Hill uses 1,000 returns (~4 years), k=100, and x_min=0.02046 in absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner fitted tails. Idealized independent-return SE (alpha/√k) is 0.338 and understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoff estimates (3.419/2.985) aren’t a confidence interval. Unchanged extremes can produce plateaus. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SOXX.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
SOXX’s 252-return DFA H rose from 0.414 (Nov 19) to 0.437 (Nov 20), below the independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. One-/five-observation changes were +0.022/+0.021. Its prior-30 standardized deviation was −0.86, not a significance test because windows overlap.

R²=0.962 measures fit only on supplied scales. Short/long H (0.420/0.525) differ: one line fits poorly across scales 8–63, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.778 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

Hill alpha fell from 3.031 (Nov 16–19) to 2.946. Lower means heavier fitted tails, higher means thinner, if the model fits. The 1,000-return window (~4 years) uses k=99 and x_min=0.0390 absolute log-return units. Independent-return SE=0.296 understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.474/2.541, not a confidence interval. Plateaus are normal when new returns miss the top 99. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

interpretation.text:

Despite R²=0.974 on supplied scales, one line fits 8–63 poorly: 0.490 at 8–20 versus 0.677 at 25–63 may reflect crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Absolute-return H=0.676 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H rose from 0.353 on Oct 12, gaining 0.038/0.092 over 1/5 observations. It’s 2.82 standard deviations above its prior-30 average; overlapping windows preclude significance testing here.

Hill alpha fell unevenly from 2.921 to 2.812 (1,000 returns, ~4 years; k=99; x_min=0.04449 absolute log-return units). Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. Independent-sample SE (alpha/√k=0.283) understates uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.254/2.824, not a confidence interval. Plateaus are normal without new top-k extremes. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SPY.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov 20, SPY’s 252-return DFA H was 0.502, near the independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.953 measures fit only across scales 8–63. Short/long H (0.472/0.572) differ: one line fits poorly across scales, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.717 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H rose 0.020/0.021 over 1/5 observations. The prior-30 standardized deviation (+0.43) is not a significance test because windows overlap. H/alpha went from 0.448/3.253 (Oct 12) through 0.527/3.400 (Nov 6) to 0.502/3.294.

Hill uses 1,000 returns, k=99, and x_min=0.01461 in absolute log-return units. With a suitable model, lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails. The independent-return standard error (0.331) understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.223/2.877, not a confidence interval. Plateaus are normal without new top-k extremes, not evidence of stasis. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
